entries.appliesTo: Idaho local school districts and public charter schools (plus duties on the state department of education and state board of education)

dutySources.risk-program: § 33-7004 — 'Each local school district and public charter school shall adopt a policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence by students and employees in school buildings, on school grounds, during school activities, and on school-issued devices.'

sources.policyRequired: § 33-7004 — 'Each local school district and public charter school shall adopt a policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence by students and employees'

flags: CODING.md rule 6's example asserts ID S 1227 'is a chatbot-safeguards bill', but the fetched engrossed text is a Generative AI in Education act (new Chapter 70, Title 33) with no chatbot/companion-AI provisions; coded from the text per rule 1. The example likely confused this bill with ID S 1297 ('Conversational AI Safety Act').

Substantial duties bind the state department of education / state board rather than schools: § 33-7003 ('The state department of education shall develop a statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework, subject to state board of education approval'), § 33-7005 (develop and recommend literacy standards, assessment guidelines, and a professional development plan), § 33-7006 ('shall develop for parents and legal guardians a generative AI guidance document'), § 33-7008 (permissive rulemaking) — public-sector-adjacent provisions inside an education bill.

§ 33-7005 duties are develop-and-recommend obligations on the department ('shall develop and recommend to the state board of education'), not direct mandates that schools teach standards or deliver training; therefore curriculum and trainingRequired params were not coded.

§ 33-7007(1) imposes a disclosure duty directly on private vendors: 'Vendors shall disclose whether products utilize machine learning, predictive analytics, or generative AI and shall provide assurances regarding data protection, algorithmic transparency, and responsible use.' This is procurement-conditioned (applies to tools 'procured by local school districts and public charter schools'), so category was kept as education rather than company; flagged because the category rule says mixed company duties normally push to company.

§ 33-7007(1) procurement requirement ('All generative AI-related software, applications, and tools procured by local school districts and public charter schools shall comply with state and federal data privacy laws') fits no education-k12 param; the compliance content is cross-referenced law (FERPA, CIPA, COPPA), not coded per the no-imports rule.

§ 33-7004(4) policy-content requirement cross-references other statutes ('Comply with all applicable state and federal laws, including Idaho student data privacy requirements, the Idaho parental rights act...') — not coded per the no-imports rule.
No penalty or enforcement provision anywhere in the chapter; exposure omitted (silence is silence).
